login() inserts a bearer token row with no expiry column and authenticate() never checks age; tokens are valid forever and there is no logout/revocation path, so a leaked token grants permanent access.
POST /auth/login has no rate limiting, lockout or backoff, so passwords (including the short 12-char generated temporary passwords) can be brute-forced online without restriction.
When the email is unknown, login returns 401 without running scrypt, but a known email incurs a full scrypt verification; the response-time difference lets an attacker enumerate registered emails.
